alignments.note: Conjunction waw rendered *And* (rule 14).
Conditional/casuistic כִּי takes the ASV's *if* (rule 55).
Anarthrous noun with supplied *a*, which belongs to the nominal expression (rule 15); head on the lexeme-bearing noun.
Finite verb with its auxiliary; head on the lexical verb (rules 17, 24). Discontinuous from *a stranger* under rule 25 by English word order.
Preposition אֵת (H854, *with*) rendered *among* (rule 11), not the object marker H853.
Pronominal suffix rendered by the object pronoun (rule 18).
Waw of the weqatal takes *and*; the verb takes the verb (rule 14).
Verb with auxiliary *will*; head on the lexical verb (rules 17, 24).
No article morpheme is present; the supplied *the* belongs to the nominal expression it determines (rule 15), head on the noun.
Preposition לְ rendered *unto* (rule 11).
Divine name.
כְּ rendered by the compound preposition *according to*, one rendering of which no morpheme owns a part (rule 30); head on the lexeme-bearing word (rule 24).
Construct noun with the supplied *the*: the ASV writes a *the* before each word, so nothing is fronted and the construct takes the supplied one (rule 29, arthrous case).
Article on the nomen rectum takes the *the* standing before its own word (rule 29).
Nomen rectum carries the relational *of* (rule 19), headed on the noun.
Waw rendered *and* (rule 14).
Second כְּ likewise rendered *according to* as one compound preposition (rules 30, 24).
Construct noun; no article morpheme stands on it, so the supplied *the* joins its unit (rules 15, 29).
Suffix as nomen rectum rendered *thereof* (rules 18, 19).
Adverbial כֵּן → *so*.
Finite verb with its subject pronoun and auxiliary; head on the lexical verb (rules 17, 24).
Noun *statute*; the numeral takes its own word.
Numeral אַחַת → *one*.
הָיָה in a possessive recasting takes the *have* itself, with its auxiliary (rule 43).
The possessive recasting *ye shall have* leaves the לְ no English word of its own (rules 40, 43).
Suffix takes the English subject pronoun of the recast possessive clause (rule 43).

The Hebrew writes a connective of its own for each coordinated member (waw before לַגֵּר and waw before לְאֶזְרַח), so the *both … and* pair is distributed rather than placed on one morpheme: this waw takes the opening *both* written where it stands (rule 14, the אוֹ … אוֹ case). The competing reading gives the whole pair to the second waw as one discontinuous unit and leaves this one unrepresented; two written connectives against two English words is what decides it, as rule 42 counts waws against *and*s.
Preposition לְ rendered *for* (rule 11).
Assimilated article supplied by MACULA as its own token takes the written *the* (rule 12).
Noun *sojourner*.
Second waw takes the closing *and* written for it (rule 14).
Preposition לְ rendered *for* (rule 11).

Anarthrous substantive recast as *him that is born*: no article or relative morpheme is present, so the supplied antecedent, relative and copula join the substantive's own unit (rules 46, 20), headed on the word carrying the lexeme.
Article on the nomen rectum takes the written *the* (rule 29).
Construct relation recast with *in*, which belongs to the nomen rectum (rule 19); head on the noun.

review_notes: The *both … and* of the closing coordination is distributed across the two written waws (s027, s031) rather than given whole to one, since each member has a connective morpheme of its own; the alternative reading is named in that unit's note.
s025 (לְ of לָכֶם) is unrepresented because the ASV recasts the clause as *ye shall have*, with הָיָה taking the *have* and the suffix the subject pronoun (rules 40, 43).
Both construct chains write a *the* before each word, so rule 29's arthrous case governs: the present article takes the *the* before its own word and the construct noun takes a supplied one.
